Build a working local panel

This guided practice uses local simulation only, never real equipment. You will use nine component types in two exercises. Tap the bright area outlined in purple; the rest of the screen is dimmed. After completing an action, tap the highlighted Next button. Tap the step counter to fold this card; use Back or Retry whenever needed.
First, tap the highlighted mode button to return to editing.
Tap the highlighted + at the top left to open the component library.
Tap the highlighted Controls heading to expand it.
Clear the search field to show the component needed for this step.
Tap the highlighted component card to add it to the canvas.
1. Add a Button
In edit mode, tap + at the top left, then tap or drag a Button from Controls onto the canvas. The LED and text display are ready to receive your first message.
2. Open its properties
Tap the Button on the canvas while editing. Its properties open below. Selecting the correct component matters: other Buttons do not complete this step.
Use the same Topic

Switch to edit mode, select the highlighted control, and set its Topic to:\n%1$s\nThe receiving components already use this Topic. Topic is the message address; payload is its content. If you changed a receiver, use Retry to inspect and correct it.
3. Send and receive
Tap Play, then press the Button. Watch the LED and text display respond. Merely entering run mode is not enough: the same message must actually be received.
4. Add a Switch
Return to edit mode. Open + and add a Switch. Unlike a Button, it maintains an on/off state; next you will connect it to the same receivers.
5. Try the Switch
Tap Play and change the Switch. Its ON/OFF payload should update the same LED and text display. This demonstrates multiple controls sharing one message address.
6. Add a Slider
Return to edit mode and add a Slider from Controls. A scale meter and line chart have been added for this exercise. Scroll down to see them.
7. Watch live values
Tap Play and drag the Slider. The scale meter follows the value and the chart adds a point. Repeat to compare current value with history. Continue after an actual numeric message is received.
8. Edit your heading
Return to edit mode. Select the Text decoration near the top and change its text content. Text is a design element; Text Display receives MQTT messages.
9. Move the Graphic
Select the purple Graphic near the top and drag it to a new position. Hold and drag the component itself, not the resize handle.
10. Resize it
With the Graphic selected, drag its bottom-right resize handle to change its dimensions.
11. Delete the Graphic
Drag that Graphic to the red delete area. Only this decoration needs to be deleted. The next step restores it with Undo.
12. Undo the deletion
Tap the Undo arrow in the top toolbar and check the Graphic returns. If the app restarted and Undo history is gone, Retry returns to the deletion exercise safely.
Ready to build your own panel

You used controls, receivers, a chart and decorations. This was local simulation, not a device connection. For real equipment, create a new project, enter your own Broker/Port/credentials and match device Topics. Never put secrets on public test brokers. Export JSON for backup before changing apps.
